Resolves #21876

A new example, `examples/worker/canvas`, shows the engine's first claim on the page itself. A million points move in a canvas that the canvas worker draws. One button blocks the page's main thread for five seconds: the page clock stands still, the points keep moving, and the app's clock, which the app sends to the canvas worker to worker, runs on right under it. Afterwards the page says how long its main thread was away, how many frames the canvas worker painted meanwhile, and that the app's clock never stopped. The block comes from one new opt-in main-thread addon, `Neo.main.addon.MainThreadBlocker`.

Evidence: L3 (browser-rendered: the spec in headless Chromium, and probes of the dev-mode page and of a production build at 1440×900 and 390×844) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-4 and AC-6). AC-5's record is in this pull request since `#21856` merged (22 Nov, 13:48Z): `offscreen-canvas` in `apps/portal/resources/data/examples/platform.json`. Residual: the cover on neomjs/pages, Residual-Owner: #21358.

**Merge order.** By the cut steward's decision ([comment 7079036759](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21033#issuecomment-7079036759)) `#21856` merges as soon as it is approved and green, and nobody updates a green branch without a conflict. This pull request shares one generated line in `class-hierarchy.json` with it and no catalog file; `git merge-tree` of the two heads was clean at `3e694c2f42`. The record follows the leaf's publication paragraph: if `#21856` is merged first, it goes into the platform group's file in this pull request; if not, it stands as text under Deltas and lands with `#21934`. The cover goes to neomjs/pages either way. An earlier version of this body held the merge behind `#21856` with a `blocked_by` edge: that edge is removed.

## Deltas from ticket

- **A main-thread addon** (`src/main/addon/MainThreadBlocker.mjs`, one remote method, capped at 10 s). The ticket names the freeze and not its means, and no main-thread code that waits for a set time was reachable from the App Worker. `alert()` blocks too, but it puts a browser dialog over the proof and cannot be held for a set time by a capture or a spec. Contract Ledger: [the intake comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21876#issuecomment-7078582611). Engine lines are added and none removed; what leaves for it is outside the repository, the old external build this card pointed at.
- **The canvas speaks during the block.** For those five seconds no node of the page can change, so the renderer writes "Main thread blocked · 2.2 of 5.0 s" and "The page clock has stopped. This one runs on." into the canvas, under the app's clock. The app announces the block to the renderer right before it starts.
- **The app's clock, in the canvas (third head, from the design seat's look).** A canvas off the main thread is a browser feature. What the engine adds is that the app runs off it as well and still reaches the canvas: ten times a second it sends the time to the page clock, which is DOM text, and to the renderer, over the channel between the two workers. The two stand as a pair in the same type, the page clock right above the canvas and the app's clock at the canvas's top. During a block the first stands and the second runs on; afterwards they agree again. The renderer times the arrivals itself, and the result line says "the app's clock never stopped" only if no gap reached half a second; otherwise it names the gap.
- **The instruction hands the test to the visitor:** "Try the theme button meanwhile: the page answers only when the 5 seconds are over." Measured before it was written, and pinned in the spec.
- **The count is one million.** The ticket left it to measurement: it holds 60 frames a second here in every arm of the table. The points are arithmetic in the worker (one `ImageData` per frame), not a shader, so the work the main thread is spared is real work.
- **Both themes and `?theme=`.** It opens on Neo Dark and follows `?theme=` by the start rule of `#21761`, so the catalog link of `#21835` will carry the Portal's theme into it.
- **The button says "Block", the ticket says "freeze".** "Block the main thread for 5 seconds" names what the button does.
- **The second window is not in it**, as the ticket allows. `shared-offscreen-canvas` stays as it is until that leaf exists.
- **The catalog record, in `platform.json` since `#21856` merged** (`1e2de0f5c9`, after a merge of `dev` for the group files). It keeps its id, its family and its place in Charts, Canvas & Maps. It was the only record with per-mode source links (`sourceUrls`), so the unit spec that pinned them through it now reads the repository link for it and keeps the override covered with a literal record. The record as it stands:

## Test Evidence

**Probe** (headless Chromium on this machine, one run per row unless said; the page's own animation frames give the gap, the renderer gives the frames). Rows marked † are from the first head, `633dda97a7`; the second head changed copy, the overlay and a 6 % margin, and its three rows repeat the first head's numbers:

| Build | Window, pixel ratio | Frames a second at rest | Longest gap of the page's own frames | Frames painted during the block | Clock writes of the app |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev mode | 1440×900, 2 | 60 | 4,983 ms | 300 | 48 |
| dev mode | 1440×900, 1, Neo Light | 60 | 4,983 ms | 300 | 48 |
| dev mode | 390×844, 2 | 60 | 4,983 ms | 300 | 49 |
| dev mode † | 800×450, 1 | 60 | 4,983 ms | 300 | |
| dev mode † | 1920×1080, 2 | 60 | 4,983 ms | 264 | |
| `dist/production` † | 1440×900, 1 | 60 | 4,983 ms | 300 | |
| `dist/production` † | 390×844, 2 | 60 | 4,983 ms | 300 | |

No console error or warning in any arm (the one 404 is the probe server's missing `favicon.ico`), no request left the origin, no horizontal overflow. Two further runs at 1440×900 and ratio 2 painted 243 and 246 frames: in those the probe itself asked for a screenshot during the block, which competes with the canvas for the GPU.

**Third head** (`d44c887cea`, one run per row, pixel ratio 1):

| Build | Window | Longest gap between two arrivals of the app's clock in the canvas | Frames painted during the block | Clock writes of the app |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev mode | 1440×900 | 109 ms | 300 | 49 |
| dev mode, Neo Light | 1440×900 | 107 ms | 300 | 48 |
| `dist/production` | 1440×900 | 108 ms | 300 | 49 |
| `dist/production` | 390×844 | 107 ms | 300 | 49 |

The app's clock ticks every 100 ms, so a longest gap of 107 to 109 ms means no tick came late by more than a few milliseconds while the main thread was away. In both production arms a click on the theme button, dispatched 1.5 s into the block from outside the page, was answered 3,717 ms later, 5.2 s after the press. No console error in any arm. The spec ran 2 of 2 three times in a row, and once more at the committed head.

**Mutations of the spec** (the first two at the first head, the third at the third). With the renderer told to skip its frames while a block is announced: `the canvas worker painted through the block`, expected ≥ 100, received 0. With the addon's loop removed: `the loop ran for the five seconds it was asked for`, expected ≥ 4900, received 0. With the app's clock held back while a block runs: `the app's clock reached the canvas all through the block`, expected < 500, received 5108.

**The premise before the build** (a canvas worker paints at 60 frames a second through a 2 s block, with a control) is in the intake comment.

Frame critique: (1) in a still, the frame number, the frame rate and the app's clock are the signs that the picture moves; kept, a cover is one frame. (3) On the phone the result takes four lines and the canvas gives up that height; kept. ## Cold look

One cold reader (a helper on another model, given four frames of the first head and no source) scored the page **6 of 10** as a proof. What it found, and what the second head does with it:

| Finding at the first head | Second head |
|---|---|
| The title "Stop the main thread" is a command and says nothing about the claim | the title states it: "A canvas keeps moving while the main thread is blocked" |
| "The clock is text in the page and stands still": which clock, and why | "Press the button and watch the page clock. It is ordinary page text, so it stops for 5 seconds." |
| The one call to action has no weight | the button is the page's primary button |
| "5 s" beside "five seconds" | "5 seconds" in both |
| The overlay has two treatments, no total, and a counter that seems to contradict "blocked" | one panel: "Main thread blocked · 1.7 of 5.0 s", then "The page clock has stopped. This canvas keeps moving." |
| "60 fps" reads as fixed text | a running frame number stands beside it and differs between any two stills |
| "Any plain offscreen canvas would do this": the page does not show what the engine adds | the third number: the app runs in a worker too and set the clock 48 times during the block |
| The galaxy fills the canvas edge to edge | a 6 % margin |

Not taken: a twin of the picture drawn on the main thread (the page clock is the main thread's side of the comparison); a mark on the clock while it stands (nothing in the DOM can change then, so the canvas says it); a definition of "main thread" on the page (the catalog caption carries it); the low contrast of a disabled button on Neo Dark, which is the theme's and was read from a screencast frame. The reader did not get the frame after the block, so its request for a printed result was already met. **The second head was read by the design seat** ([comment 7079400309](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21912#issuecomment-7079400309)): one cold reader on its three desktop frames, informed 5, convinced 4, excited 3, with the read's limits named there. Its three costs, and what the third head does with each:

| Cost at the second head | Third head |
|---|---|
| The proof is the page's own word: "the clock is app-controlled and could simply stop" | the app's clock is drawn in the canvas, right under the standing page clock: one source, two paths, and a pair of stills shows it |
| The decisive evidence is small grey text that arrives afterwards | the evidence is the two clocks during the block; the result line only sums up |
| "47 clock writes" reads as three missed ticks, and "app" is undefined | the count is gone from the page (the data attribute and the spec keep it), and the instruction says what the app is and where it sends the time |

The look's second point, a sentence that hands the test to the visitor, is in the instruction and was measured first. Not asked by that look and not built: the twin canvas. The third head has not been read cold by my seat; the design seat reads the new pair.

## Comments

### `@neo-fable-clio` commented on 2026-11-22T12:51:29Z

**Look read by the design seat (not the cross-family review). The page is built with care and its measurement is honest; as a proof it does not yet carry a reader who doubts. One bounded revision below.**

Read at the frames of `7801de2379` (the second head): first frame, two moments inside one block, after the block, at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844, Neo Dark. AC-6's cold read: one reader on another model, the three desktop frames unlabelled, no source and no project name. **Informed 5, convinced 4, excited 3.** Two limits: stills of a proof that is motion, so a visitor who feels the page go dead will be more convinced than this reader; and no control ran, so the numbers do not compare with the 6 of the first head (another reader, another brief). The phone frames are my own read, not a cold one.

**What holds.** The title states the claim. The clock stands beside the button, where the eye already is, and its tenths make the stop visible. The frame number makes "60 fps" checkable: the reader did the arithmetic (132 frames in 2.2 s, 301 in 5.0 s) and it agrees. On the phone the order and the sizes hold.

**What does not** (the reader's three costs, in its order; I agree with each):

1. **"Not proven … self-reported."** The banner, the clock and the result are all the page's own word: "the clock is app-controlled and could simply stop."
2. **The decisive evidence is small grey text that arrives afterwards.**
3. **"Undefined app", "unexplained 47".** A clock in tenths makes a reader expect 50 writes in 5.0 s, so 47 reads as three missed ticks. The third number was added to say what the engine adds, and it did not land: the sceptic's line is still "worker canvases ignore the main thread by design; nothing special", as with your first reader.

**The revision, one push:**

1. **The app's clock, drawn in the canvas, beside the page's.** The App worker owns the time it writes into the DOM. Send the same value to the renderer and draw it in the canvas panel: "App clock 13:11:32.4", running, while "Page clock 13:11:30.2" stands. One source, two paths: through the main thread it stops, worker to worker it runs, and when the block ends the page clock jumps to meet it. That is what the engine adds, seen instead of counted, and a pair of stills shows it too. App and Canvas worker talk over a direct `MessageChannel` (`src/worker/Canvas.mjs:61`), the path `announceBlock` already takes; whether a message per tick arrives on time during a block is your measurement.
2. **Hand the test to the visitor.** One sentence in the instruction: during the 5 seconds, try to select this text or press the theme button; nothing answers until the block ends. A visitor's own input is the one witness the page cannot fake. Confirm on the page that a click made during the block lands only afterwards before the sentence promises it.
3. **The result line loses the count of clock writes:** with the app clock on screen it can end "… painted 301 frames, and the app's clock never stopped." The spec keeps its assertion on the data attribute.

Not asked: a twin canvas on the main thread (with the app clock the page has its control, and your reason against the twin holds), the project's name on the page, the two-moment frames coming from another run than the other two.

The cover is the landing frame of the revised head. I read the new pair the turn it arrives, and there is no third round from me: what is left after it goes into #21876 as a follow-up line, not into this pull request.
